1.name: Pump housing
1.spec: Round body with two port bosses, four through-bolts to the end plates
1.note: Holds the liner, takes air in on one side and blows it out the other. It mounts on the engine's accessory pad and turns 1.3 times engine speed.

2.name: Liner
2.spec: Ø54 bore, 4.5 mm off the rotor's axis, two port windows
2.note: The hard ring the vanes sweep. Its bore is off-centre from the rotor, so each pocket between two vanes grows on the inlet side and shrinks at the outlet.

3.name: Rotor
3.spec: Ø44.9 × 40, six radial slots, splined bore
3.note: A dry pump runs with no oil: the rotor and vanes are carbon, which lubricates itself. It also wears and is brittle, which is how dry pumps fail.

4.name: Vane
4.note: Thrown out against the liner as the rotor turns, each vane seals one pocket from the next. A broken vane jams the pump and shears its coupling.

5.name: Drive shaft and shear coupling
5.spec: Splined, with a nylon coupling to the engine's drive
5.note: Turns the rotor. The coupling is the weak link on purpose: if the pump seizes it shears, so the engine is saved and only the vacuum is lost.

6.name: Regulator body, cap and screen
6.spec: Inlet from the instruments, outlet to the pump, adjusting screw
6.note: The pump makes far more suction than the gyros need at cruise. The regulator lets outside air in through its foam screen to hold about 5 inHg.

7.name: Regulator poppet
7.spec: Ø12 disc closing a Ø8 seat from below, guide stem
7.note: Outside air presses on it through the seat; past 5 inHg that push beats the spring and it opens, about 0.4 mm at cruise.

8.name: Regulator spring
8.spec: 0.15 N/mm, set by the screw to crack at 5.0 inHg
8.note: Its preload is the setpoint: 0.85 N against the seat's area is 5.0 inHg. Its low rate keeps the suction nearly flat as the pump speeds up.

9.name: Central air filter
9.note: All the air the gyros breathe comes through here. A clogged filter starves them and shows as low suction; dust in the bearings shortens their life.

10.name: Lines and fittings
10.spec: Hose 9.5 ID, brass barbed fittings and tee
10.note: Filter to the instrument cases, cases to the regulator and pump, pump overboard. A leak lets in air that never passed the jets.

11.name: Suction gauge
11.note: The only sign of the vacuum system's health. Low suction means slow rotors, so a sluggish horizon and a wandering heading.

12.name: Instrument case
12.note: Sealed so the air can only enter through the filter line and the jets. The vacuum gyros' cases are under suction; the electric one's is not.

13.name: Attitude gyro rotor
13.spec: Ø44 brass, turbine buckets on its rim, 21 000 rpm
13.note: Spins about the vertical. Its 0.11 N·m·s of angular momentum keeps it upright in space while the aeroplane rolls and pitches round it.

14.name: AI rotor housing (inner gimbal)
14.spec: Can round the rotor, pitch pivots, vane unit below, two jets
14.note: Carries the rotor's bearings and the two jets that drive it; its pitch pivots let it stay level as the nose rises. The used air leaves through the vane unit.

15.name: AI outer gimbal
15.spec: Frame on fore-and-aft pivots in the case
15.note: The roll gimbal: the case rolls round it in a bank. The air comes in through its rear pivot and down its side to the housing.

16.name: Pendulous vane
16.spec: Hung over each of four exhaust slots, 0.5 sheet
16.note: Hang plumb and half cover their slots. If the rotor tilts, one slot opens and its jet's reaction precesses the rotor back: erection.

17.name: Horizon card and bank pointer
17.spec: Sky and ground card on the gimbals, pitch ladder
17.note: Held level by the gyro while the case, and the little aeroplane on it, bank round it. The pointer on its top reads the bank on the fixed scale.

18.name: Heading gyro rotor
18.spec: Ø42 brass, buckets on its rim, 18 000 rpm
18.note: Spins about a horizontal axis that holds its direction in space, so the case can turn round it and show the turn as a heading.

19.name: HI rotor housing (inner gimbal)
19.spec: Can round the rotor, pivots across its axis
19.note: Lets the rotor stay level as the aeroplane pitches and banks. Torque on its pivots precesses the rotor in heading: that is the drift.

20.name: HI vertical gimbal and crown gear
20.spec: Ring on vertical pivots, crown gear on its lower end, the air jet
20.note: Turns about the vertical inside the case as the aeroplane turns; its crown gear drives the card. Its jet blows on the rotor's buckets.

21.name: Compass card, shaft and pinion
21.spec: Card on a fore-and-aft shaft, bevel pinion on the crown gear
21.note: Shows the gimbal's angle as a heading under the lubber line. It only knows directions in space, not north: it must be set to the compass.

22.name: Heading-set knob
22.spec: Push to engage its gear with the crown gear, turn to set
22.note: Pushed in and turned, it turns the gimbal and card to the magnetic compass's heading, cancelling the drift; every 15 minutes or so.

23.name: Turn coordinator gyro motor
23.spec: Outside-rotor 14 V DC motor, Ø34 bell, 9 000 rpm
23.note: Electric, so it keeps working when the vacuum fails. Its spin axis lies across the aeroplane; H = 0.008 N·m·s.

24.name: TC gimbal and spindle
24.note: A turn makes the gyro precess about this axis. Canted 30°, it also feels the roll into a turn, so the needle leads the bank.

25.name: Centring spring
25.spec: Pair, between the gimbal and the case
25.note: Turns precession into a reading: the gimbal tilts until the springs' torque balances H·Ω, so the tilt is the rate of turn.

26.name: Damper
26.spec: Air dashpot on the gimbal's lower post
26.note: Damps the gimbal to about 0.7 of critical so the needle settles without swinging in rough air.

27.name: Miniature aircraft
27.spec: On the face, worked by the gimbal through a linkage
27.note: Its wingtip on the L or R mark is a standard-rate turn, 3°/s, two minutes for a full circle. It shows rate, not bank.

28.name: Inclinometer
28.spec: Curved glass tube R 45, agate ball, damping fluid
28.note: The ball sits where gravity and the turn's pull balance. Centred: coordinated. Out of the turn: a skid. Into it: a slip. Step on the ball.
